MINUTES OF THE REGULAR MEETING
  CITY OF NORWALK PARKS AND RECREATION COMMISSION
  January 8, 2026

Chairperson Victor H. Juan called the meeting to order at 6:01 p.m.
Commission members present were Anthony Armendarez, Alejandra Hernandez, David
King, Don Valenzuela, Victor H. Juan, and Briana Martinez. Commissioner Maria Carbajal
and Monique Yanez were absent.

Staff Present included Director of Recreation and Park Services Allan Perdomo,
Recreation Superintendent Sonia Batres, Recreation Supervisor Maurisabel Camacho,
Recreation Supervisor Pati Garcia, and Office Assistant II Vanessa Piceno.

APPROVAL OF MINUTES

Commissioner Martinez motioned to accept the December 11, 2025 meeting minutes.
Commissioner Armendarez seconded the motion. All in favor.

REPORTS
2025 Artastic Final Event Plan Discussion

Recreation Supervisor Pati Garcia presented the Parks and Recreation Commission an
update on Artastic 2026. The presentation outlined event activities, staffing needs, and
new program elements. Staff reviewed the Chalk Art Competition, which will include three
age and professional categories and require five judges, with four positions still available.
Judging will begin at 6:00 p.m., followed by the awards ceremony at 7:30 p.m. A sign-in
sheet was passed around to identify those commissioners interested in serving as judges.
A new Drum Circle activity was introduced, which will require volunteer assistance to
distribute instruments and support participating children. Additional event components
include Art Walk vendors, ARTBOX artists, and the introduction of a Sensory Room. Staff
noted that the Cultural Arts Center Division will collaborate with the Adaptive Recreation
team to develop inclusive activities for the Sensory Room. The presentation concluded
with no questions from the commission.

Park Projects Monthly Update

Director Allan Perdomo provided a comprehensive update on current and upcoming park
improvement projects. He reported progress on field lighting renovations, Park field
renovations, facility improvement updates were provided, including completed HVAC
work at the Cultural Arts Center and ongoing HVAC and solar panel installations at the
Norwalk Arts and Sports Complex, Aquatics Pavilion, and Well 10. Staff outlined the
Hermosillo Park Rehabilitation, Stormwater Capture, and Infiltration Project, noting that
demolition will begin on January 12, 2026, and that community meetings are scheduled

monthly, with the next meeting and open house taking place on January 21, 2026. The
Holifield Park Master Plan timeline was reviewed as well sharing that the first out of six
community engagement meetings will be on January 24, 2026. Lastly, staff reported that
the Camera and Wi-Fi Project have been completed at all parks except Robert White
Park, and that welded sign installations are largely complete, with remaining installations
scheduled for early 2026. All questions were addressed following the presentation.

STAFF COMMENTS

January is a slower season. A fitness expo will take place this weekend from 10:00 a.m.
to 1:00 p.m., and 5K registrations will be raffled off. Pee Wee Basketball registration is
now open. We are also offering teen résumé and job application reviews. Seasonal
positions are expected to open in 1–2 weeks, with in-person interviews for selected
candidates. Seasonal positions are open to the public. Youth worker positions are open
only to Norwalk residents and applicants may not be related to City employees.

COMMISISONER’S COMMENTS

Commissioner King – Mentioned that the Las Posadas event had a great turnout, and
he that he really liked the band.

Commissioner Hernandez – Shared that the Holiday events were great. Holidays at
the Hargitt was very enjoyable, especially with the different decor. She is looking
forward to comparing the tours in the summer and would like to see Teatime offered in
the spring. On Monday, December 22, 2025, she attended the Hermosillo Park
Community meeting, which had approximately 50 people in attendance. Participants
were very passionate, and she commended the Recreation and Park Services
Department Director for maintaining a calm demeanor throughout the meeting. She
suggested adding microphones or enhanced sound for future meetings. Some
attendees expressed frustration about the lack of communication with the community in
the past and would like to see improvements in outreach and engagement for the
Holifield Park project. She noted that the agenda for the meeting was well organized
and provided suggestions for future meetings of this nature. She believes WRD can
provide valuable insight and serve as positive advocates in their role. noted that funding
was not available last year but has since been secured.

Commissioner Armendarez – He shared that he is excited for the Artastic sensory
rooms and requested that social media messaging highlight the availability of this activity
at the event. He expressed appreciation for the installation of lighting and cameras, noting

January 8, 2026

that they are greatly needed. He plans to attend the sports expo and hopes to see
colleagues there. Regarding the extravagant egg hunt, he requested that the possibility
of having public safety staff at the gates be explored, as the release of children was
chaotic last year.

Commissioner Valenzuela – He shared that he is looking forward to the upcoming
programs and is excited about what’s to come in the new year. He also mentioned that
he would like to see a visual for the Hermosillo underground water project to better
understand the process.

Commissioner Martinez – Shared that she enjoyed Las Posadas because it was warm
and welcoming. She felt spoiled by all the areas that were offered, including crafts, food,
a photo booth, candy, and more. TAP did very well and she commended the staff for
keeping the space clean throughout the event. It was nice to see the community being
supported and the city hosting such a meaningful event.

Commissioner Juan – Shared that he received an email regarding the Brown Act from
City Clerk’s office and was looking to confirm if all commissioners reviewed this email as
well. He also gave props for improving the Holifield park outreach meeting schedule and
marketing.

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
N/A
NEXT MEETING
February 12, 2026

There being no further business to discuss, Chairperson Victor H. Juan motioned to
adjourn the meeting. Seconded by Commissioner Martinez. All in favor. The meeting was
adjourned at 6:57 p.m.
Respectfully submitted,

__________________________
Chairperson Victor H. Juan
